title: Winter is coming (for your wallet)
gist: Resolution Foundation's weekly note says the UK cost of living squeeze is about to worsen: CPI hit 3.1% in August, the Bank of England sees 4% this winter with the energy price cap tipped to rise by a quarter in January, while real pay growth is only 0.6% and private sector pay (2.8%) lags public sector pay (6.0%). It also flags revised hours data halving the productivity puzzle, Norwegian evidence that self-made rich out-invest old money, and an inconclusive AI-jobs literature.

insights.claim: UK CPI inflation rose to 3.1% in August after a 12p-a-litre jump in petrol prices, and the Bank of England forecasts inflation of 4% this winter.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Rising UK inflation into winter limits room for BoE cuts; bearish for front-end gilts and real incomes.
insights.quote: Inflation climbed to 3.1 per cent in August following a 12p-a-litre jump at the pumps

insights.claim: The UK energy price cap is tipped to rise by a quarter in January, deepening the winter cost of living squeeze.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Energy retailers' revenues rise while discretionary consumer spending comes under pressure in Q1.

insights.claim: The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% and changed how it unwinds QE, which cut gilt yields by roughly 10bps on announcement, worth about £900 million to the government.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Slower or restructured QT is a gilt-supportive lever; watch further BoE balance-sheet tweaks as fiscal pressures build.
insights.quote: gilt yields dropped roughly 10bps on announcement, worth about £900 million
insights.locator: The Bank offered some glimmers of hope

insights.claim: UK real regular pay growth is hovering at 0.6% and set to weaken as inflation climbs, while unemployment has held at 4.9% even as payrolled employees and vacancies drift down.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Falling real pay plus a softening labour market points to weaker UK consumer demand into winter.
insights.locator: Not such great news for workers

insights.claim: UK private sector pay growth fell to 2.8% in July and typical private weekly pay is worth £2 less in real terms than last October, while public sector pay growth is running at 6.0%, partly due to earlier NHS pay settlements.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: A two-speed wage picture: private sector real squeeze already under way, public sector pay a fiscal pressure point.

insights.claim: Strong public sector wage growth creates a challenge for next year's Spending Review, including a £1.8bn unfunded teachers' pay settlement left by Rachel Reeves, now set for a £500m top-up, forcing a choice between pay restraint, squeezed services or higher taxes.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Adds to UK fiscal pressure and the likelihood of further tax rises or public service cuts.
insights.quote: So, who will take the strain?
insights.locator: Strong public sector wage growth also presents

insights.claim: The state pension is set to rise 3.9% in April under the triple lock, which Resolution Foundation's chief executive publicly called "crazy".
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: The triple lock is a growing fiscal cost and a potential target for reform; retirees are shielded while private workers are squeezed.
insights.locator: All eyes were on this week’s wage data

insights.claim: About half of the UK's post-financial-crisis productivity puzzle now appears to evaporate because hours worked had been overestimated, meaning fewer hours per job rather than declining output per hour explains more of the weak growth.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Total output, living standards and revenues are unchanged, but the revision reframes UK growth diagnostics toward labour input rather than efficiency.
insights.quote: about half the UK’s productivity puzzle is now thought to evaporate

insights.claim: In 26 years of Norwegian tax data, 'Old Money' in the top 0.1% already held 26 times average household wealth in their 20s and grew mainly via inheritance (42%) and saving (31%) with 8.5% annual returns, while 'New Money' started from minus 0.1 times average wealth and grew on 18% annual returns and 22 times more labour income.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Self-made wealth is driven by high-return concentrated investing and labour income, relevant for wealth management targeting and wealth-tax design.
insights.quote: the self-made rich are out-investing, and out-working, the aristocrats

insights.claim: An LSE review of 74 studies on AI's impact on employment or wages finds results diverge so widely that a study exists to support any narrative, with 70% of the literature relying on potential exposure evidence rather than observed job effects.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Treat confident AI job-loss or job-boom claims skeptically; exposure-based studies are weak evidence of realised impact.
insights.quote: You can find a study to support whichever story you want to tell, so be wary anyone claiming to know the answer.

insights.claim: A Social Market Foundation survey finds the best UK career pathway yields almost £30k higher earnings by age 35 than the worst; young workers whose first job built confidence earned 24% more later, and interns were more than twice as likely to land on the best pathway.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: First-job quality compounds into lifetime earnings; policies like a Good First Job Guarantee would shift training costs onto employers.

insights.claim: Evidence from 43,000 German workers over 35 years shows working at least two hours a week more than desired hurts wellbeing roughly half as much as unemployment and does not fade over time; over a third of European workers want shorter weeks.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Persistent overwork costs support demand for flexible or shorter-hours arrangements, relevant to productivity and retention.
insights.locator: Burning (out) the candle at both ends.
